summary: Guard the packaging validator against interpreters without tomllib

delivery.outcome: The managed agent-host validator imports on any interpreter the adopted standard allows, so a repository declaring requires-python >=3.10 no longer fails its own gate with a false missing-validator defect.
nonGoals: No change to what the packaging bindings require on interpreters that can read TOML.
No new runtime dependency: tomli is used only when it is already installed.

architecture.decision: Import tomllib defensively (stdlib, then an already-installed tomli, then None) and skip the Python packaging binding when no reader exists. governance_check.py treats an ImportError from this module as a missing managed file, so the import must never fail; interpreters at 3.11+ keep enforcing GOV-PACKAGING-001/002/003 unchanged.
architecture.rollback: Revert the commit; the import returns to the unguarded stdlib form.
